{{Short description|Mathematics educator}}
'''Gilah Chaja Leder''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM|FASSA}} (born 1941) is an adjunct professor at [[Monash University]] and a professor emerita at [[La Trobe University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.education.monash.edu.au/profiles/gleder |title=Adjunct Professor Gilah Leder |access-date=2010-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110219035109/http://www.education.monash.edu.au/profiles/gleder |archive-date=2011-02-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Her research interests are in mathematics education, gender, affect, and exceptionality. Leder was the 2009 recipient of the [[Felix Klein Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/news21.html |title=Felix Klein Medal for Gilah Leder |access-date=2010-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101227113810/http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/news21.html |archive-date=2010-12-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life==
She was born in 1941, during the II World War, in [[Hilversum]], [[North Holland]]. Being a Jewish child, she was hidden and protected by the catholic Zwanikken family of [[Laren, North Holland|Laren]]. The father of the house, Cornelis Zwanikken worked at the municipality department of Social Affairs. Here, she was accepted as one of their own and affectionately called “zusje” (little sister). She learned to read and write in her early childhood. After the war she was reunited with her family. They started to live in Netherlands, where she visited coeducational elementary school. In November 1953 she moved to [[Adelaide]], Australia. She started her 7th grade there at Woodwille High School, a coeducational government school. She got her bachelor's degree with honours in mathematics at [[University of Adelaide]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=u7nqH3RzUusC&pg=PA118&lpg=PA118#v=onepage&q=Gilah%20Leder|title= Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary]</ref><ref>[https://catalogue.gleneira.vic.gov.au/cgi-bin/spydus.exe/FULL/WPAC/BIBENQ/3890971/21401613, Courage to care : 28 remarkable stories of rescue during World War II 2016]</ref>

==Career==
She started her career teaching maths at a high school in [[Melbourne]]. Later she was offered a position at Melbourne Secondary Teachers College.
After having given birth to her 2 children, she completed her PhD and a doctorate at Monash University. Later she was appointed as a lecturer in the Faculty of Education at Monash University.

In 1990 she edited and published a journal ''Mathematics and Gender'' together with [[Elizabeth Fennema]].
In 1993 she was named Monash's University 'Supervisor of the Year' for her talent in supervising postgraduate students.
In 1994 she was appointed a professor of Education at La Trobe University.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=u7nqH3RzUusC&pg=PA118&lpg=PA118#v=onepage&q=Gilah%20Leder|title= Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary]</ref>

In 2010 she was honoured by the [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction]] for her achievements in mathematics education, research and development.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latrobe.edu.au/bulletin2/winter-2010/people/global-maths-medal-for-gilah-leder|title=Global Maths Medal for Gilah Leder|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228100658/http://www.latrobe.edu.au/bulletin2/winter-2010/people/global-maths-medal-for-gilah-leder|archive-date=2018-02-28|url-status=dead|date=Winter 2010|magazine=La Trobe University Bulletin}}</ref>

She was elected a Fellow of the [[Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia]] in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Academy Fellow: Emerita Professor Gilah Leder AM, FASSA|url=https://socialsciences.org.au/academy-fellow/?sId=0032v000033l9QGAAY|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-10|website=Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia|language=en-US}}</ref> She is past President and life member of the Mathematics Research Group of Australasia and of the International group of Psychology of Mathematics Education.

Leder was made a [[Member of the Order of Australia]] (AM) in the [[2019 Queen's Birthday Honours (Australia)|2019 Queen's Birthday Honours]] in recognition of her "significant service to higher education, and to the Jewish community of Victoria".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2004488|title=Professor Gilah Chaja Leder|website=honours.pmc.gov.au|access-date=2019-06-10}}</ref>

==Publications==
Leder has almost 200 scholarly publications,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/news21.html |title=Felix Klein Medal for Gilah Leder |access-date=2010-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101227113810/http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/news21.html |archive-date=2010-12-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref> including:

* Mathematics and gender: Changing perspectives. Handbook of research on mathematics teaching and learning: A project of the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics. Leder, Gilah C. In Grouws, Douglas A. (Ed). (1992). ''Handbook of research on mathematics teaching and learning: A project of the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics.'' (pp.&nbsp;597&ndash;622). New York, NY, England: Macmillan Publishing Co, Inc.
